subject.title: Codex turn fails with generic Telegram fallback when invalid image tool model is configured, leaving child agent orphaned on full stdout pipe

question: Should invalid explicit media-generation model refs fail during config/startup, be converted into clear user-facing runtime errors, or remain runtime-only with improved Telegram diagnostics?
rationale: The source evidence shows missing preflight and generic fallback behavior, but changing validation strictness, Telegram error disclosure, and Codex cleanup guarantees affects user-visible config and process-lifecycle policy.

options.title: Preflight explicit refs plus clear fallback
options.body: Validate explicit media-generation model refs before the turn when possible, and surface a stable Telegram error/log pointer for runtime-only failures.

options.title: Runtime-only diagnostics
options.body: Keep config loading permissive and improve the user-facing runtime error, accepting that invalid refs may still start a turn before failing.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open without design changes until a current Telegram/Codex live repro proves the orphaned-pipe failure still happens.

recommendation.title: Preflight explicit refs plus clear fallback
recommendation.body: Validate explicit media-generation model refs before the turn when possible, and surface a stable Telegram error/log pointer for runtime-only failures.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent history in explicit image-generation defaults and Telegram behavior, which are the two highest-signal owner boundaries for the product decision.
